slots.title: September CPI due at 12:30 p.m. ET
slots.body:
Headline CPI for September is on the calendar for Oct. 14 at 12:30 p.m.
ET.

Economists’ median calls in the data feed point to year-over-year inflation at 3.6%, up from 3.4% in the prior reading.

Month-over-month headline inflation is estimated at 0.6%, versus 0.4% last time.

“Core” inflation — prices excluding food and energy — is estimated at 2.5% year-over-year (prior 2.4%) and 0.2% month-over-month (prior 0.3%).

Asian markets were positioning ahead of the print; the Nikkei 225 finished up 0.6% at 68,193.13 in the latest overseas snapshot in the feed.

What number would you treat as the line-in-the-sand for the core year-over-year read?

slots.title: Oil up as Mideast tensions headline
slots.body:
Brent crude in the feed: $106.48, +0.7% on the session.

The United States Oil Fund ($USO) closed at $153.09, +1.4%.

Reuters reported the Trump administration plans to expand a Delek Texas refinery using the Defense Production Act — a separate energy-policy headline from the same window.

CNBC linked the oil move to growing Middle East tensions between Iran-backed Houthis and Saudi Arabia, including reports of coalition strikes on energy terminals and fuel reserves in Yemen.

Which headline do you weight more for near-term energy prices — refinery policy or the Yemen–Saudi story?

The session low was 245.19; the high was 256.18.

Healthcare was among the weaker groups on Nasdaq, with the sector average down about 1.7%.

slots.title: U.S. cash session — Oct. 13, 2026
slots.body:
The S&P 500 ended essentially flat, down less than 0.1% at 7,805.37.
The Nasdaq Composite slipped 0.2% to 27,204.38.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average lost 0.3%, closing at 51,670.10.
The Russell 2000 was off 0.4% at 2,783.37.

At 2 p.m.
ET the Census release showed September existing home sales at 3.99 million units annualized, above the 3.95 million estimate and up 1.5% month over month versus a -0.3% estimate.
The prior month was -3.2%.

Large banks reported throughout the day.
JPMorgan posted EPS of 5.75 versus 5.93 expected and revenue below the estimate; the stock closed down 0.9% at 331.43.
Citigroup beat on EPS and revenue but fell 5.6% to 124.53.
Wells Fargo beat EPS at 1.87 versus 1.85 but revenue missed; shares lost 3.1% at 80.74.
Goldman Sachs reported EPS of 17.01 versus 12.86 expected and finished down 0.2% at 891.91.

Johnson & Johnson beat on EPS and revenue yet dropped 5.7% to 248.61.
UnitedHealth beat with EPS of 4.69 versus 4.14 expected and closed down 0.2% at 377.76.
AbbVie lost 2.4% to 274.31; Eli Lilly slipped 1.4% to 1,166.51.
The Nasdaq healthcare sector average was down about 1.7%.

On the upside in megacaps, Oracle rose 4.2% to 143.22.
Advanced Micro Devices gained 1.9% to 605.53.
Salesforce added 1.7% to 238.01.
Microsoft ticked up 0.4% to 543.45.
Communication services was the strongest Nasdaq sector in the table, up about 1.3% on average; technology averaged about 1.1% higher.

Energy names moved with firmer oil.
Chevron rose 1.3% to 217.84 and Exxon Mobil 1.2% to 174.13 while the energy sector average gained about 1.8%.
Brent crude settled up 0.7% at 106.45; the USO ETF rose 1.4% to 153.09.
Industrials averaged about 1.8% lower on Nasdaq; real estate about 1.6% lower.

Domino’s Pizza reported EPS of 4.60 versus 4.36 expected and revenue above estimate, but the stock still fell 4.8% to 296.10.
Albertsons beat on EPS and revenue and closed up 1.4% at 12.72.

The VIX edged up 0.4% to 15.27.
Gold futures rose 0.3% to 4,190.80.
The UUP dollar proxy slipped 0.4% to 29.02.
Bitcoin was up 0.8% at 83,767.70.
Treasury yields in the injected snapshot (dated 2026-10-09) showed the 10-year at 5.2% and the 2s10s spread at 0.44 percentage points.

Overseas indexes in the bundle included the Nikkei 225 up 0.6% at 68,193.13 and the Hang Seng up 0.2% at 24,397.00; the FTSE 100 was down 0.1% at 10,650.33.
